claim: flag of 'Cars and trucks, used' is consistent with the Directive
note: second-hand goods sold by taxable dealers are taxed on the dealer's margin (Arts. 311-325), private sales are outside the scope: a Directive reading is ~0.1, not 1/2. 1/2 = dealer sales taxed on the full price (a sales-tax rule). It is the post's own flag (sharply pinned by Fig 4) and NOTES/us_flags.csv say so, but the judgment-call table still heads all flags 'EU Directive reading'

claim: flag of 'Water and other public services' is consistent with the Directive
note: water supply by public bodies is taxable (Art. 13 + Annex I(2)); sewerage and refuse collection by public authorities are outside the scope unless competition is distorted. CE merges water with sewerage, so 0.688 taxes sewerage (Nordic practice) and exempts refuse; a strict reading would be lower, the Nordic one 1.0. Choice between 0.688 and 1.0 pinned by the $249 dividend: documented

claim: flag of 'Rented dwellings' is consistent with the Directive
note: letting of immovable property exempt (Art. 135(1)(l)), tenant insurance exempt (135(1)(a)), tenant-paid repairs taxable: 0.017 is a correct reading, but 0 (the post's 'rent exempt') is equally Directive-consistent and fits the printed Fig 4 numbers better

claim: flag of 'Home maintenance, repairs & insurance' is consistent with the Directive
note: repair services and materials taxable (Annex III(10a) allows reduced rates), homeowners insurance exempt (135(1)(a)), ground rent = letting of land (135(1)(l)). Condo/HOA management fees (4.9% of the line) are exempt or outside in some member states

claim: flag of 'Other lodging' is consistent with the Directive
note: hotel accommodation is carved out of the letting exemption (Art. 135(2)(a)) so taxable; vacation-home interest, taxes and insurance are not taxable supplies; school housing exempt (letting, or 132(1)(i))

claim: flag of 'Vehicle rental, leases, licenses' is consistent with the Directive
note: registration, vehicle property tax and licences are taxes or public-authority fees (Art. 13); vehicle inspections (1.7% of the line) are also treated as public fees, though private test centres charge VAT in most states

claim: flag of 'Miscellaneous' is consistent with the Directive
note: legal, accounting, funeral (Annex III(16)) taxable; lotteries (135(1)(i)), bank charges (135(1)(d)), credit interest (135(1)(b)), union and professional dues (132(1)(l)) exempt; taxes outside

claim: flag of 'Housekeeping supplies' is consistent with the Directive
note: postage by the universal service provider exempt (Art. 132(1)(a))

claim: flag of 'Education' is consistent with the Directive
note: tuition exempt (Art. 132(1)(i),(j)); books and supplies taxable

claim: flag of 'Fees and admissions' is consistent with the Directive
note: simplification: Art. 132(1)(m) (sport by non-profits) and (n) (cultural services of public or recognised bodies) exempt part of this line; taxing all of it is the post's uniform-base reading (club memberships exempt, 0.71, fits Fig 4 worse)

claim: flag of 'Public and other transportation' is consistent with the Directive
note: passenger transport taxable (Annex III(5)); some states keep exemptions under Art. 371/Annex X and international air is effectively zero-rated (airline fares are 60% of this line)

claim: flag of 'Other household expenses' is consistent with the Directive
note: taxable services (internet, gardening, pest control, moving); housekeeping paid to household employees (13.6% of the line) is a wage, not a supply

claim: flag of 'Vehicle maintenance and repairs' is consistent with the Directive
note: repairs and parts taxable; the 'auto repair service policy' (5.2%) is exempt insurance when a third-party insurer sells it (CJEU C-349/96)

claim: flag of 'Drugs' is consistent with the Directive
note: medicines are goods: taxable, reduced rates allowed (Annex III(3)); some states zero-rate Rx

claim: flag of 'Personal services (incl. childcare)' is consistent with the Directive
note: child and elderly care by recognised bodies exempt (Art. 132(1)(g),(h))
